sections.markdown:
## C — Rules for pedestrians, entering from alleys and driveways, left turns and U-turns, red-light running and Traffic Survival School, yielding to and following emergency vehicles, the move-over law, funeral processions and stopping for school buses
Knowledge domain: how to stay safe when you are the pedestrian, who yields when you leave an alley or turn left or make a U-turn, what happens after a red-light conviction, how to yield to and follow emergency vehicles, the move-over law, funeral processions, and when to stop for a school bus.

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal with all lights dark, you may proceed with caution if the crosswalk is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
When you are the pedestrian, you can often see an approaching vehicle more easily than its driver can see you, especially at night, at dusk and dawn, and in bad weather. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
As a pedestrian, never assume an approaching vehicle has seen you and will yield. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians should use crosswalks where they exist or cross at an intersection. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Whenever possible, a pedestrian should make eye contact with the drivers of approaching vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Look before stepping into the road, because even at a crosswalk drivers need time to notice you and react. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians should avoid distractions such as phones, headphones or earbuds while crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
At night, cross in a well-lit spot, and always follow the traffic rules, signs and signals where you cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
When you drive out of an alley or driveway onto the road, you must stop before reaching the sidewalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
After stopping at the sidewalk, yield to pedestrians and to approaching vehicles before entering the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
When turning left, you must yield to any oncoming vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A01
A U-turn is allowed when you can make it safely, it will not get in the way of other traffic, and no sign forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A01
When making a U-turn, yield to approaching traffic and turn only when it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A01
A citation for running a red light or another civil traffic violation may make you eligible for the Arizona Supreme Court's Defensive Driving Program, so read the papers that come with the citation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A02
A conviction for running a red light or a flashing red light means you must attend Traffic Survival School. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A02
MVD is told when you finish Traffic Survival School successfully, and no further court appearance is then required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A02
If running a red light causes a crash resulting in life-threatening injuries to another driver or passenger, you may face a fine up to five hundred dollars, a three-month driving-privilege suspension, and court-ordered community service [A02].
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A02
If you cause a crash in which another driver or passenger dies, you may be fined up to $1,000, have your driving privilege suspended for six months and be ordered to do community service. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
By law, MVD must order Traffic Survival School for every red-light conviction the courts report. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
A red-light conviction also adds points, which appear on your driver record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A02
Paying the fine means accepting responsibility for the violation, and it is reported to MVD as a conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A02
Not completing Traffic Survival School leads to an indefinite suspension of your driving privilege. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A02
Stay alert for emergency vehicles, especially at intersections. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A02
When a police car, fire engine, ambulance or other emergency vehicle approaches with a siren, lights or other warning device, yield, move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A02
On a four-lane highway with at least two lanes going the same way as the emergency vehicle, proceed with due caution and yield by moving into a lane that is not next to its lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A02
If that lane change is impossible or unsafe, proceed with due caution and reduce your speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A02
Keep at least 500 feet behind a fire department vehicle that is responding to an emergency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A02
Keep at least 300 feet behind a police vehicle that is responding to an emergency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A02
Do not drive into or park in the block where an emergency vehicle has stopped to respond to an emergency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A03
The move-over law requires you to shift over one lane to leave a safe margin when you pass any vehicle with flashing lights stopped at the side of a road or highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A03
If moving over is unsafe or impossible, you must slow down and use caution instead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A03
The move-over law covers every pulled-over vehicle with flashing lights, including emergency-response and police vehicles, tow trucks, highway maintenance vehicles and private vehicles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A03
The move-over law applies on all freeways and other multi-lane highways and on city roads and streets. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A03
You must yield to any vehicle in a funeral procession led by a funeral escort vehicle flashing a red or blue light. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A03
When you approach a school bus that is picking up or dropping off passengers, stop completely before reaching it, whichever direction you are traveling. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A03
A school bus loading or unloading passengers shows alternating flashing lights and an extended mechanical stop-sign arm. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A03
Stay stopped until the school bus moves on or until its stop-sign arm and flashing lights are withdrawn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A03
Watch for children crossing in front of or behind a stopped school bus, since a child may dart out from either end. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A03
On a divided roadway you do not have to stop for a school bus when you are traveling in the opposite direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F40 | anchor: A03
A divided roadway is separated by a physical barrier such as a fence, curbing or a gap in the pavement; painted striping alone does not count. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F41 | anchor: A03
On a divided roadway you may proceed with caution past a school bus in the approaching lanes, but not past one stopped on your side of traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec10-F42 | anchor: A03
Every speed regulation must be obeyed, and you should be prepared to change your speed quickly when needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0039]

Misconceptions: a school bus on the other side of a road divided only by painted lines still requires you to stop, because striping is not a physical separation; paying a red-light fine is not a way to avoid a conviction, it counts as one; a fire truck and a police vehicle call for different following distances; the move-over law covers private cars and tow trucks with flashing lights, not just police.
Mnemonics: Fire five, police three — hundreds of feet behind; bus arm out, everybody stops unless a barrier divides the road.
Glossary: Traffic Survival School means the course MVD must order after a red-light conviction; Defensive Driving Program means the Arizona Supreme Court course some cited drivers may attend; divided roadway means a road split by a physical barrier; funeral escort vehicle means the lead vehicle of a procession flashing a red or blue light.
Dynamic facts: fines, suspension lengths and Traffic Survival School rules are set by statute and can change, and eligibility for the Defensive Driving Program is explained in the papers that come with each citation.
